content.introduction: In August 2026, the US stock market is experiencing a sector rotation with Healthcare leading, as indicated by a 12-month return of 16.0% driven by attractive valuation, low volatility, strong earnings, and expansion in the GLP-1 obesity drug market. Meanwhile, the technology sector is facing concentration risk as capital shifts from mega-cap tech stocks to cyclical sectors like Energy, Healthcare, Financials, and Industrials. In August 2026, the US stock market is undergoing a profound sector rotation. The technology-led rally that has dominated since 2023 is gradually broadening into Energy, Healthcare, Financials, and Industrials. This "market breadth broadening" trend signals that capital is rotating out of highly concentrated mega-cap tech stocks into more attractively valued cyclical sectors. More on diversification can be found in our portfolio diversification guide and Sharpe ratio tutorial. [...] Algo Lab

# August 2026 US Stock Sector Focus: Healthcare Leads, Tech Rotation

August 2026 sector rotation: Healthcare leads while Tech faces concentration risk. Algo Lab models track capital flows and key signals.

## August 2026 US Sector Rotation Overview [...] Healthcare (XLV) led all sectors in August 2026 with a 12-month return of 16.0%. Key drivers include attractive valuation (~18x forward P/E), low volatility profile (Beta 0.65-0.75), strong Q2 2026 earnings beats, and continued expansion in the GLP-1 obesity drug market.

### Is tech still worth investing in during August 2026?

Importantly, this looks less like panic and more like healthy rebalancing. Investors are repositioning toward reasonable valuations and sectors with real earnings support, rather than fleeing risk entirely. Industrials have benefited from the same AI data-center build-out powering energy, while cost-conscious consumer spending has lifted defensive staples names.

## Why Is Healthcare One of the Most Interesting Turnaround Plays? [...] Healthcare deserves its own mention because it may be the most interesting turnaround candidate. The sector was a dead weight for years — near-flat returns in 2023 and 2024 — before improving late in 2025 and edging ahead of the broad market this year (Fact Set, July 20, 2026). A big part of the re-rating is reduced policy risk: new drug-pricing agreements and caps on pharmaceutical import costs have taken some of the worst-case scenarios off the table, even though tariff questions on patented [...] on patented drugs remain a genuine wildcard. Layer in demographic tailwinds and AI-driven efficiencies in drug development, and several strategists now flag healthcare as one of the few places offering broad value in an otherwise fully priced market.

Practically speaking, our continuing allocation to value and low volatility stocks moves the portfolio slightly away from the AI theme, and more towards other parts of the market, which should also benefit from the AI-led productivity gains that are anticipated to occur across much of the economy (with some early evidence from the national accounts data that this productivity boost is indeed starting to take shape).
